Did you know?

  • The cashier remembers London at holiday time as her favourite way to celebrate.
  • The final solution mixes a first class ticket with an economy return.

📖Read the text اقرأ النص

صفحة 33 من الكتاب — محطة القطار من الداخل

Read

00:00 / 00:00 اسحب على الشريط للتنقّل · اضغط أى كلمة فى النص للانتقال إليها

Part 1 — "I would like to buy a train ticket" Man: Excuse me, Miss. I would like to buy a train ticket. Cashier: Well you are in the right place. Where are you going? Man: I am going to London. I am visiting my family there for the holidays. Cashier: That is wonderful! I went to London once during the holiday season. It was my favourite way to celebrate. Man: I am not looking forward to it. I love London and I miss my family, but it is quite jammed this time of year. The streets, buses, trains, and airports will all be busy. Cashier: I’m sure it is very stressful. I am looking for an available ticket for you now. Do you want to depart tonight? Man: If I can, I want to leave either tonight or early tomorrow morning. I’m hoping to get home before dinner tomorrow. My grandmother is cooking and I can’t miss that!

Read

00:00 / 00:00 اسحب على الشريط للتنقّل · اضغط أى كلمة فى النص للانتقال إليها

Part 2 — First class or economy? Cashier: Let me see what I can do to get you home in time for dinner. Hmmm … ok. I am sorry, sir. I do not have an available ticket in economy class until 11:45 AM tomorrow morning. However, there is an available first class ticket at 7:00 PM this evening. Man: How much is the first class ticket? Cashier: It is one-hundred pounds. Man: Is that a round-trip ticket? Cashier: No, sir. That is one way. Man: That is costly! I don’t know what to do. I told my grandmother I would be home for dinner. Cashier: Well, you can buy a one-way ticket first class and book a return ticket in economy class to save some money. Man: That is a great idea! Thanks, I will do that. Cashier: Glad I could help. I hope you enjoy your holidays. Just give me one more minute to hand you a printout and you will be on your way home soon.

❓Answer the following questions أجب عن الأسئلة الآتية

1- What does "Miss" (line 1) refer to?
اعرض الإجابة
It refers to the cashier — the young woman selling the tickets at the station.
2- Where is the man travelling to?
اعرض الإجابة
To London, to visit his family for the holidays.
3- The cashier and the man have different points of view about London this time of year. Explain referring to the text.
اعرض الإجابة
The cashier loved London during the holiday season and calls it her favourite way to celebrate, while the man is not looking forward to it because the city is jammed and the streets, buses, trains and airports will all be busy.
4- Why does the man need to leave as soon as possible?
اعرض الإجابة
Because he hopes to get home before dinner the next day — his grandmother is cooking and he cannot miss it.
5- What is the difference between "economy" and "first class" tickets?
اعرض الإجابة
Economy class is the cheaper one, but no seat was available until 11:45 AM the next morning; first class costs one hundred pounds and a seat was available at 7:00 PM the same evening.
6- How did the cashier help the man solve his problem?
اعرض الإجابة
She suggested that he buy a one-way ticket in first class and book the return ticket in economy class to save money.

⚖️Write (True) or (False) صح أم خطأ مع التصحيح

صفحة 35 من الكتاب — لندن ليلًا ونهر التيمز

Correct the false statements.

1- A first class ticket is a hundred dollars.
اعرض الإجابة
False — It is one hundred pounds, not dollars.
2- The man is going to spend the holidays with his friends.
اعرض الإجابة
False — He is going to spend them with his family; his grandmother is cooking dinner for him.
3- The cashier helps the man to travel to London on the same day.
اعرض الإجابة
True
4- A round-trip ticket is less expensive than a one-way ticket.
اعرض الإجابة
False — The one-way first class ticket alone costs one hundred pounds, so a round-trip ticket costs more.
5- The man decides to cancel the trip to London.
اعرض الإجابة
False — He accepts the cashier’s idea and buys a first class ticket with an economy return.

📝Complete the paragraph أكمل الفقرة الآتية

صفحة 36 من الكتاب — عجلة لندن الشهيرة London Eye

Use words from the text to complete the paragraph below.

Booking a ……………… to London during the holidays is almost impossible. It is either you spend your saving on a ……………… ticket or cancel the trip altogether. To avoid a ……………… and annoying holiday, try to make reservations, book a ticket long before the holidays season, have a confirmed ……………… of the ticket in your pocket and enjoy your holiday.

اعرض الإجابة
Booking a ticket to London during the holidays is almost impossible. It is either you spend your saving on a first class ticket or cancel the trip altogether. To avoid a stressful and annoying holiday, try to make reservations, book a ticket long before the holidays season, have a confirmed printout of the ticket in your pocket and enjoy your holiday.

❓Think and discuss فكّر وناقش

صفحة 36 من الكتاب — برج الساعة Big Ben والبرلمان
1- What do you prefer: spending a holiday with your family or friends?
اعرض الإجابة
I prefer spending my holiday with my family. Friends are fun, but a holiday is the only long time I get to sit with my parents and grandparents without school or work. I can travel with my friends any weekend, but family time is harder to find.
2- Some families are in the habit of spending the holidays abroad. What do you think of that?
اعرض الإجابة
Travelling abroad opens the mind: you meet other cultures, practise languages and see famous places. However, it is very costly and it takes families away from their relatives during the feast. I think a family should travel abroad sometimes, but not every holiday.

🖊️Writing التعبير الكتابي

صفحة 38 من الكتاب — بطاقة بريدية من لندن
  • Writing a postcard
  • Start the postcard with: Dear + the person’s name.
  • Use the present continuous for what you are doing: I am having a great time here in London.
  • Use the present perfect for what you have done: I have visited the Tower of London and Big Ben.
  • Use "going to" for future plans: Tomorrow, we’re going to watch a play at the theatre.
  • Finish with a nice wish (Wish you were here!) and end with: Love + your name.
  • You are spending the holidays in London. Follow the given outline to write a postcard to one of your friends in New York.
